_comment: This is rulesync 16.6.0's CANONICAL schema, not Claude Code's native one. The event key is camelCase `preToolUse` (rulesync maps it to `PreToolUse` on generate), and each definition is FLAT -- matcher/type/command as siblings -- because rulesync builds the nested {matcher, hooks:[{type,command}]} shape itself. The top-level `hooks` record is required by rulesync's Zod schema even though only the claudecode override carries content: every per-tool override block, `claudecode` included, is wrapped in z.optional() and this one is not. BOTH FAILURE MODES BELOW WERE RE-MEASURED ON THE PINNED VERSION, side by side against the version pinned before it, and NEITHER MOVED -- the major bump changed nothing here. MODE 1, THE NESTED SHAPE. Feed it Claude Code's native PascalCase/nested shape and stderr warns `Skipped hook event(s) for claudecode (not supported): PreToolUse` -- but `Skipped` is the WARNING's word, not the OUTPUT's, and believing it is how this file shipped inert once already. The override block is merged in UNFILTERED (only the shared `hooks` record is filtered to supported events) and an unmapped event name passes through VERBATIM, so `PreToolUse` lands at exactly the path Claude Code reads. There `type` defaults to `command` when absent, and the emitted command is read from the definition's OWN `command` field -- which the nested shape has not got, because the real command sits in an inner `hooks` array rulesync never looks in. What lands is {matcher: Bash, hooks: [{type: command}]}: well-formed, correctly placed, and carrying no command at all. THE COUNT GATE IS BLIND TO THIS ONE -- the full file set is written, the `+ 1 hooks` summary term is present, and guard_rulesync_drift.py exits 0. Only guard_emitted_outputs.py reds, which is the whole reason it reads structure rather than counting. MODE 2, OMITTING THE TOP-LEVEL `hooks` KEY. generate prints a Zod error, exits 0, and still writes every other output -- CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/agents/, .claude/skills/ -- under the ordinary `All done!` summary, with ONLY .claude/settings.json missing. The Zod error goes to STDERR, and CI pipes only STDOUT into the drift guard -- so what actually reds that guard is the `+ 1 hooks` term going MISSING from the summary, not the error text. Both gates catch this one. A CORRECTION THIS FILE USED TO CARRY, AND THE REASON TO MEASURE ON A FRESH TREE. An earlier note here recorded that under a much older version the same omission wrote nothing at all and printed `All files are up to date`, and called that an inversion in the dangerous direction. IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Re-run against that version on a FRESH tree -- under the `-t` list in force when it was pinned as well as today's -- and it behaves exactly as described above: exit 0, every other output written, only settings.json missing, and no `up to date` line anywhere. The likeliest origin is the trap guard_rulesync_drift.py names in its own prose: rulesync SKIPS a file whose content already matches, so a run in an ALREADY-GENERATED tree prints `All files are up to date` whatever the input says. Wipe the outputs first or the measurement is worthless. So the honest record is that mode 2 has held its shape across every version tested. Re-measure on the next bump regardless -- both modes exit 0 under an ordinary summary, and THAT is what makes a change in either invisible; not that one has moved before. WHAT EACH GATE IS FOR. scripts/guard_rulesync_drift.py compares the emitted counts against a pinned map and sees the hooks feature expected but absent -- in mode 2 only. scripts/guard_emitted_outputs.py reads the emitted .claude/settings.json STRUCTURALLY -- it requires a command that RUNS the guard to sit at hooks.PreToolUse[*].hooks[*] with type command, the one path Claude Code executes -- so it fails closed both when the file is absent and when the file looks right but the command is gone. Not a grep: a grep proves only that the string is somewhere in the document, and a command re-nested under another event, carried on a non-command hook, or merely echoed satisfies it while running nothing. AGAINST A HUMAN EDIT, tests/test_hooks_wiring.py pins this shape and this comment is only a courtesy. AGAINST A RULESYNC VERSION BUMP, this comment is the FIRST defence and no longer the only one: the offline suite asserts THIS file, so a rulesync that renamed `preToolUse` or re-nested the definitions would leave it green -- but the emitted-output guard reads the generated ARTIFACT, so it catches the dropped command whatever the input schema was renamed to. Re-verify the emitted .claude/settings.json by hand when changing the pinned version in package.json.
